title: The Vault
tagline: A premium AI lab portfolio — part showcase, part workshop, part operating system for experiments.
description:
- Most portfolios are static galleries.
- I wanted mine to be a living lab notebook — a place where each project has depth, context, and a story.
- I also wanted to dogfood my own tools: build a system that makes it easy to add new projects, and use it as a sandbox to learn new technologies.
- The goal was to create something that feels more like a product than a portfolio.

questionnaire.problem:
- Most portfolios are static galleries.
- I wanted mine to be a living lab notebook — a place where each project has depth, context, and a story.
- I also wanted to dogfood my own tools: build a system that makes it easy to add new projects, and use it as a sandbox to learn new technologies.
- The goal was to create something that feels more like a product than a portfolio.
questionnaire.whyMattered:
A portfolio is never really done, so I wanted to build something I'd enjoy maintaining and iterating on.

- Most project galleries show only the result, not the thinking behind it.
- I wanted each project to feel like a mini case study.
- Building it publicly also pushed me to ship things I'd otherwise leave unfinished.

It became a reflection of how I work: fast, iterative, and focused on craft.
questionnaire.howBuilt:
I started by exploring WebGL shaders — the Bioluminescence and Aurora backgrounds were built first, just to see what was possible.

Then I built the project system:
- Designed a questionnaire-based workflow so adding a project feels like answering a short interview.
- Used drag-and-drop reordering because the order of projects always changes.
- Added a full-screen presentation mode with animated slide transitions for each project.
- Built a command palette (⌘K) for quick navigation because I use it on every site I visit.

**Tech Stack:**
- **Next.js 16** with App Router
- **TypeScript** + **Tailwind CSS v4**
- **Framer Motion** for spring-powered animations
- **Three.js / @react-three/fiber** for WebGL backgrounds
- **@dnd-kit** for drag-and-drop sorting
- **Supabase** for persistence
- **Lucide** for icons

The whole thing was built iteratively — each new feature was an excuse to learn something I hadn't tried before.
questionnaire.biggestChallenge:
The WebGL backgrounds took the most experimentation.

- Writing GLSL fragment shaders that look good across different GPUs and screen sizes.
- Making the bioluminescence effect feel organic and responsive to mouse movement.
- Balancing visual quality with performance so the site stays smooth.
- Building the Digital Rain preloader with wave physics and ripple effects.

On the product side, the hardest part was designing the questionnaire flow — turning open-ended answers into a structured project page without making the process feel like a form.
questionnaire.outcome:
- A fully functional portfolio that doubles as a project management system.
- Six published projects with rich presentation content.
- A repeatable workflow for adding new projects in minutes.
- WebGL shader skills that I can reuse in future creative projects.
- Deep understanding of Next.js App Router, Supabase, and modern React patterns.
- Dogfooding confirmed: I actually enjoy updating this site.
questionnaire.improveNext:
- **Creative Coding** — WebGL shaders, GLSL, Three.js
- **Next.js App Router** — server components, API routes, parallel routes
- **Drag-and-drop UIs** — dnd-kit, sortable contexts, custom handles
- **AI-assisted Development** — using LLMs for rapid prototyping
- **Design Systems** — building a consistent visual language from scratch
- **Product Thinking** — designing tools that make future work easier
